title: Redwood discovery — reliability & fallbacks (Lumen Medical)
summary: Exploratory discovery on reliability, multi-region routing, and fallback policies across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for Lumen Medical's HIPAA-adjacent workloads; agreed to run a short pilot and share security docs and pricing.
action_items: Evelyn Park: send Dedicated pricing sheet and pilot proposal (due 2026-08-21)
Marco Diaz: propose perf benchmark plan and sample workload template (due 2026-08-24)

next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, ISO, audit logs) and KMS integration notes

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-19 15:00 PDT | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Evelyn Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sara Chen (CTO - Lumen), Dev Patel (Platform), Maya Ortiz (Head of AI)
[00:00] Evelyn: hey everyone thanks for joining. we're running 45 minutes, quick intros, then Marco will run through reliability options and we'll dig into your constraints.
[00:22] Sara: thanks, Evelyn. quick context — Lumen is building an assistant for clinicians; PHI-lite but still very sensitive. latency matters for the UI, but availability is critical.
[00:32] Marco: got it. high level, Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Hosted is fastest to onboard, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, Private is full VPC/on-prem for strict controls.
[00:50] Dev: curious about failover — if a region goes down, what actually happens? we need near-zero downtime for our main flows or at least graceful degradation.
[01:05] Marco: two things — routing and fallbacks. we can do multi-region routing with automated failover; requests can be re-routed to another region or to a lower-cost tier. e.g., if your primary region has a capacity issue, we failover to a secondary region running a compatible model. there are trade-offs: cross-region adds latency, and model variants can have slightly different quality.
[01:35] Maya: how do you handle model variant differences? we can't have hallucination regressions in clinical text.
[01:43] Marco: we recommend pinning a primary model and a compatibility map — compatible variants are validated by Redwood. also quality monitoring and evals tied to prompt sets help catch regressions. we also support automatic fallback policies: for severe incidents we can degrade to a smaller, verified model or return a cached prefix while indicating degraded mode to the app.
[02:05] Sara: prefix caching's interesting. if we hit a downstream overload, can the UI still get partial responses instead of an error?
[02:12] Marco: yes — KV cash — sorry, KV cache — keeps token-level state and can return cached continuations for repetitive flows. for new prompts, we can fall back to embeddings+rerank where appropriate.
[02:30] Evelyn: question on SLA — what guarantees do you offer for hosted vs dedicated?
[02:36] Marco: hosted has a standard SLA for availability in our gateway, but Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. typical Dedicated tier SLA is 99.9% for throughput windows, with options to move to 99.95% for enterprise contracts. exact numbers depend on committed capacity and region coverage.
[03:02] Dev: 99.9% still sounds like 8+ hours a year in worst case, for us that's maybe acceptable for async but not for the live clinician flow. what sort of SLOs do customers get for P95 latency?
[03:15] Marco: P95 depends on model and batch size; for small chat models on Dedicated we often see 150–300ms P95 for single-token latency in optimized runtimes, but end-to-end generation for a 200-token response is obviously higher. we can run benchmarks with your prompts to give more precise numbers.
[03:42] Sara: also encryption — we need KMS + HSM for keys, and audit logs for every request. is that available?
[03:50] Marco: yes. Private and Dedicated support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and full audit logging. Hosted can also support customer KMS for encryption at rest for enterprise customers. we'll include the security pack.
[04:05] Maya: any constraints around data residency? some of our hospitals need data kept in-region.
[04:12] Marco: multi-region routing respects region policies. Private gives you the most control. For Hosted we can pin to region endpoints and disable cross-region failover if that's a hard requirement, though that reduces availability in case of regional incidents.
[04:30] Dev: what about graceful degradation strategies? e.g., during a failover window, can we degrade to a smaller quantized model to keep latency but lower quality?
[04:40] Marco: absolutely — Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles and model variants by workload. Fallback policies can be configured to switch to a quantized or smaller model, reduce max tokens, or switch to cached responses. you can also set a fallback to a low-latency embeddings flow that returns ranked candidates.
[05:05] Sara: do you support canary rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions?
[05:11] Marco: yes — the Console has rollout primitives: canary deploys, A/B tests, automatic fallback on error budgets or quality regressions tied to your eval sets.
[05:30] Evelyn: some questions we typically get: who owns the failover orchestration — is it Redwood or the customer app?
[05:37] Marco: Redwood manages routing and can do automated failover at the infra layer. customers can also implement app-level fallbacks — both can be used together. we surface hooks and tracing so you can see why a request was routed a certain way.
[05:55] Maya: about testing — can you run a simulated region outage and show how failover behaves?
[06:02] Marco: yes, part of the pilot we'd run fault-injection tests and perf runs. we'll instrument tracing and token-level cost breakdowns so you can see impact.
[06:18] Dev: curious about cold-starts and KV cache repopulation across regions — is there state sync?
[06:25] Marco: KV cache is local to serving instances; for cross-region failover you will experience some cold-start cost as caches are rebuilt. for heavy flows we recommend sticky routing or global caching layers for prefixes. it depends on your access patterns.
[06:45] Sara: any examples of customers with similar requirements?
[06:50] Evelyn: we have customers in health and finance who use Dedicated and Private for stricter requirements. we'll redact names in the security pack but include case notes.
[07:05] Maya: compliance-wise — SOC2, ISO, and audit trails are available? and do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[07:12] Marco: yes to all. Private gives you most control; Dedicated includes RBAC and SAML SSO integrations. we'll attach the compliance matrix.
[07:30] Dev: licensing and pricing question — if we commit to Dedicated, how does burst capacity work during incidents?
[07:37] Marco: Dedicated has autoscaling policies plus optional burst capacity. you can configure burst pools to handle spikes; we price burst separately or as part of a larger commit. we'll include a sample pricing scenario.
[07:55] Sara: what about network egress costs for cross-region routing? that could be significant and needs to be surfaced.
[08:03] Marco: yes, egress is a factor. our proposals include egress estimates based on expected throughput and region pairs. for Private, if everything is in-region there's no cross-region egress.
[08:20] Evelyn: quick check — are there any hard limits on model architectures or is Redwood supporting custom models?
[08:27] Marco: we support curated open models and customer models in Private/Dedicated depending on compatibility; for Hosted we surface vetted models. custom models on Private on-prem is doable with some onboarding work.
[08:44] Sara: we want to avoid quality regressions when switching models during failover. is there a way to guarantee a sanity check?
[08:51] Marco: we can run deterministic evals on candidate variants as part of a rollout and enforce thresholds; if a variant fails, automatic rollback or route to a safe fallback.
[09:05] Maya: timeline question — we need a decision in ~6 weeks to meet production Q1. what's typical eval length?
[09:12] Evelyn: pilot length depends on scope; a focused perf pilot with 1–2 weeks of load and quality checks is common. a broader POC including compliance onboarding can be 4–6 weeks.
[09:30] Dev: security docs — do you provide pen test results and third-party audits?
[09:36] Marco: we'll include summary info; third-party audit reports are available under NDA.
[09:50] [10:00–20:00 summarised negotiation and specifics: back-and-forth on commit sizes, rough QPS estimates, and region choices. highlights:]
[20:05] Sara: our primary region is US-West, backup would be US-East; we want failover within 30s ideally; is that realistic?
[20:14] Marco: 30s is achievable for routing-level failover; user-perceived latency will depend on whether you accept cross-region latency increases and whether caches need rebuilding. we can aim for automated route switch within 10–30s and progressively warm caches.
[20:34] Dev: what about routing by policy — can we route low-latency requests to Dedicated but batch background jobs to cheaper hosts?
[20:41] Marco: yes — smart routing by policy (latency, cost, region, tier) is supported; you can tag requests and route accordingly, with automatic fallback to compatible variants.
[21:00] Sara: if a region is flaky but not fully down, do you do partial traffic shifting?
[21:06] Marco: yes — traffic shaping and canary % adjustments are supported. you can set thresholds for error budgets to trigger automatic shifts.
[21:22] Maya: curious about observability during incidents — what do we get?
[21:28] Marco: Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdown, tracing hooks, and error analysis. during incidents we push alerts and provide logs for post-mortem.
[21:48] Dev: will logs contain PII or PHI? we need to control retention and redaction policies.
[21:56] Marco: we allow configurable retention and redaction; Private/Dedicated give more options; we'll include specifics in the security pack.
[22:10] Evelyn: let's talk about an example failover flow — primary model in US-West goes unhealthy, route switches to US-East smaller model, UI shows degraded mode and a warning. devs accept some quality drop but not hallucinations.
[22:25] Sara: ok we want a staged approach — first try route to same model in East, then smaller model, then cached responses.
[22:32] Marco: that sequence is supported and can be codified in a fallback policy: retry window, region failover, model downgrade, cache fallback.
[22:48] Maya: how do we validate hallucination risk quickly?
[22:52] Marco: we run targeted evals on your prompt set and monitor semantic drift; set thresholds for automatic rollback.
[23:05] [23:05–30:00 more technical deep dive by Marco about kernel selection, batching and quantization — occasional mis-transcriptions like "KV cash" and "Redwood Devoted" appear]
[30:12] Marco: for inference, our runtime does kernel selection based on sequence length distribution, continuous batching, and quantization-friendly paths. that helps lower tail latency.
[31:00] Dev: can we get a runbook for incident responses? who do we call during an outage?
[31:07] Evelyn: for Dedicated and Private we provide an on-call contact and escalation matrix; included in enterprise package.
[31:20] Sara: any downtime windows for patching?
[31:25] Marco: we try to use canaries and rolling updates; Dedicated customers can choose maintenance windows.
[31:40] Maya: one more — regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets, can we set custom thresholds?
[31:45] Marco: yes. we emit regression alerts and tie them to evals; you can tune sensitivity.
[32:00] [32:00–40:00 discussion of pilot specifics — sample dataset, metrics to collect (P95, error rate, token cost), and billing model for pilot]
[40:05] Evelyn: recap of next steps — we'll send pricing, security docs, and a pilot plan. Marco will propose a perf test template.
[40:18] Sara: confirms ,please include egress estimates and a runbook for the pilot.
[40:25] Dev: ask for an SLA example contract.
[40:30] Marco: will attach sample SLA and Dedicated commitment scenarios.
[40:40] Maya: okay. timeline — can we get materials by Friday next week?
[40:45] Evelyn: yes, we'll aim for EOD Friday 2026-08-21.
[40:52] Sara: thanks, this was helpful.
[41:00] Evelyn: thanks all, we'll follow up with documented next steps and schedule the pilot kickoff.
[41:08] [Meeting ends]

Auto-generated summary (optional): Lumen has strict availability and compliance requirements. Preferred approach is Dedicated with multi-region failover but they are evaluating trade-offs between cross-region latency and availability.
